finding.claim: Broken authorization on DELETE /projects/:id: the boolean result of authorized() is discarded, so any authenticated user can delete any project they do not own. Sibling PUT handler uses the throwing authorize() correctly.
finding.source: Authenticated low-privilege user supplies req.params.id of another user's project

trace.note: project loaded by id with no ownership scoping
authorized() returns a boolean (defined at lines 12-14, does not throw); return value ignored

finding.guards_checked: authorized() result unused; no throw, no if/return; no other middleware visible in repo (single file). Contrast: PUT at line 25 calls authorize(), which throws 403. Non-existent id would also yield undefined project and a TypeError at line 18/19 (500), not a guard.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean and is called as a bare statement at api.js:18, so it has no effect. The throwing authorize() at api.js:4-10 is used only in the PUT handler at api.js:25. No other middleware or auth exists in the repo, which is the single file api.js.
verdict.reason: At api.js:18 the boolean result of authorized() (defined at api.js:12-14, no throw) is discarded, so api.js:19 deletes any project for any authenticated user, unlike the PUT handler, which calls the throwing authorize() at api.js:25.
